chunks: 4 - My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd b. Abdillah narrated to us, he said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa narrated to us, he said: al-Abbas b. Ma'ruf narrated to us [from Abdullah b. al-Mughira], he said: Abu Hafs al-Abdi narrated to us, from Abu Harun al-Abdi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When you ask Allah, Mighty and Exalted, ask Him for the means to me. So I asked the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) about the means, and he said: It is my rank in Paradise. It consists of one thousand steps. Between each step is the travel distance of a galloping horse for a month. It ranges from a step of jewel to a step of chrysolite, a step of ruby to a step of gold, to a step of silver. It will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and set up with the ranks of the prophets, and it will be among the ranks of the prophets like the moon among the stars.

No prophet, saint, or martyr will remain on that day without saying: 'Blessed is he whose rank this is.' Then, a call will come from Allah, Mighty and Exalted, heard by the prophets and all of creation: 'This is the rank of Muhammad.' I will then come forward, and on that day I will be wrapped in a gown of light, wearing the crown of sovereignty and the wreath of honor. Ali ibn Abi Talib will be before me, carrying my banner — the Banner of Praise — upon which is written: 'There is no god but Allah; the successful are those who prevail through Allah.' When we pass by the prophets, they will say: 'These are two Angels of Proximity; we do not know them and have not seen them before.' When we pass by the angels, they will say: 'These are two commissioned prophets.' This continues until I ascend the ranks with Ali following me. When I reach the highest rank, with Ali one rank below me, no prophet, saint, or martyr will remain without saying: 'Blessed are these two servants — how Allah has honored them!' Then a call will come from Allah, Majestic is His Majesty, heard by the prophets, the saints, the martyrs, and the believers: 'This is My Beloved Muhammad, and this is My Friend Ali. Blessed is he who loves him, and woe to he who hates him and lies against him.'

Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: On that day, there will not remain a single person who loved you — O Ali — except that he will find relief in these words, his face will be illuminated, and his heart will be gladdened. And there will not remain a single person who opposed you, warred against you, or denied your right except that his face will be darkened and his feet will tremble.

While I am in this state, two angels will approach me. One of them is Ridwan, the treasurer of Paradise, and the other is Malik, the treasurer of the Fire. Ridwan will come forward and say: 'Peace be upon you, Ahmad.' I will say: 'Peace be upon you, angel. Who are you? How beautiful is your face and how sweet is your fragrance!' He will say: 'I am Ridwan, the treasurer of Paradise, and these are the keys of Paradise. The Lord of Glory has sent them to you, so take them, Ahmad.' I will say: 'I accept that from my Lord. Praise be to Him for what He has honored me with. Give them to my brother Ali ibn Abi Talib.'

Then Ridwan will return, and Malik will come forward and say: 'Peace be upon you, Ahmad.' I will say: 'Peace be upon you, angel. Who are you? How unpleasant is your face and how adverse is your appearance!' He will say: 'I am Malik, the treasurer of the Fire, and these are the reins of the Fire. The Lord of Glory has sent them to you, so take them, Ahmad.' I will say: 'I accept that from my Lord. Praise be to Him for what He has honored me with. Give them to my brother Ali ibn Abi Talib.'

Then Malik will return, and Ali will come forward with the keys of Paradise and the reins of the Fire until he stands at the edge of Hell, with its sparks flying, its roar rising, and its heat intensifying. Ali will be holding its reins, and Hell will say to him: 'Pass over me, O Ali, for your light has extinguished my flames.' Ali will say to it: 'Be still, O Hell! Take this one and leave that one. Take this enemy of mine and leave this friend of mine.' On that day, Hell will be more obedient to Ali than any one of your servants is to his master — if he wishes, he takes it to the right, and if he wishes, he takes it to the left. On that day, Hell will be more obedient to the commands of Ali than all of creation.

key_terms.الوسيلة: al-Wasila — the means or station; refers specifically to the Prophet's highest rank in Paradise
key_terms.رضوان: Ridwan — the angel who is the treasurer and gatekeeper of Paradise
key_terms.لواء الحمد: the Banner of Praise — the standard carried by Ali on the Day of Resurrection, inscribed with the testimony of faith
key_terms.مالك: Malik — the angel who is the treasurer and gatekeeper of Hellfire
key_terms.مفاتيح الجنة: the keys of Paradise — entrusted by God to the Prophet, who delegates them to Ali
key_terms.مقاليد النار: the reins/bolts of the Fire — entrusted by God to the Prophet, who delegates them to Ali

ai.seo_question: What does Islam teach about al-Wasila and Ali's role on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: The Prophet describes al-Wasila — his rank of a thousand steps of precious jewels in Paradise — and the Day of Resurrection procession where he and Ali walk among prophets and angels. The Prophet receives the keys of Paradise and the reins of Hell from Ridwan and Malik respectively, delegating both to Ali, who then commands Hell with absolute authority, directing it to take the enemies and spare the friends of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa narrated to us. He said: al-`Abbas b. Ma`ruf narrated to us from `Abdullah b. al-Mughira. He said: Abu Hafs al-`Abdi narrated to us from Abi Harun al-`Abdi from Abi Sa`id al-Khudri.

He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said: When you ask Allah, ask Him for the means to me. So, the Prophet (s) was asked about the means, so he said: It is my rank in Paradise. It consists of one thousand degrees, between each degree of which is the travel distance of one month on a horse – from a degree of jewel, to a degree of aquamarine, to a degree of ruby, to a degree of gold, to a degree of silver. It will be brought forth on the Day of Resurrection and installed with the degrees of the prophets. It will be to the degrees of the prophets as the Moon is to the stars.

There will not be a prophet, saint, or martyr on that day except that he says: “Blessed is he to whom these degrees belong.” Then, a call will come from Allah, which will be heard by the prophets and all of creation: “These are the degrees of Muhammad”. I will then proceed, and on that day, I will be wearing a gown of light, with a crown of rulership and a wreath of dignity. `Ali b. Abi Talib will be in front of me, with my banner in his hand, which is the Banner of Praise. On it, it is written: “There is no god but Allah. The successful are those who prevail by Allah”. When we pass by the prophets, they will say: “These are two Angels of Proximity. We do not recognize them, nor have we seen them before.” When we pass by the angels, they will say: “These are two commissioned prophets”, until I ascend the degrees with `Ali following me. Once I reach the highest of its degrees, with `Ali under me by one degree, there will not be a prophet, saint, or martyr that day except that he will say: “Blessed are these two servants. How Allah has blessed them!” Then, a call will be made from the direction of Allah, which will be heard by the prophets, the saints, the martyrs, and the believers: “This is My Beloved, Muhammad, and this is My Friend, `Ali. Blessed is he who loves him, and woe to he who hates him and lies against him.”

Then, the Messenger of Allah (s) said: On that day, there will not remain one person who loves you – O `Ali – except that he will be relieved by these words. Their faces will be illuminated, and their hearts will be gladdened. There will not remain one person who opposed you, warred against you, or denied your right except that their faces will be darkened, and they will stomp their feet.

Two angels will come to me – one of them will be Ridwan, the treasurer of Paradise, and the other will be Malik, the treasurer of the Fire. Ridwan will come forward and say: “Peace be with you, Ahmad.” I will say: “Peace be with you, angel. Who are you? How beautiful is your face and how sweet is your fragrance!” So, he will say: “I am Ridwan, the treasurer of Paradise, and these are the keys of Paradise. The Lord of Glory has given it to you, so take it, Ahmad.” So, I will say: “I accept that from my Lord. Praise be to Him for what He has ennobled me with. I give it to my brother `Ali b. Abi Talib.”

Then, Ridwan will go back, and Malik will come forward and say: “Peace be with you, Ahmad.” So, I will say: “Peace be with you, angel. Who are you? How unpleasant is your face and how adverse is your appearance!” So, he will say: “I am Malik, the treasurer of the Fire, and these are the reins of the Fire. The Lord of Glory has given it to you, so take it, Ahmad.” So, I will say: “I accept that from my Lord. Praise be to Him for what He has ennobled me with. I give it to my brother `Ali b. Abi Talib.”

Then, Malik will go back, and `Ali will come forward with the keys of Paradise and the reins of the Fire until he stands at the mouth of Hell, with its sparks flying, its roar amplifying, and its heat intensifying. `Ali will be holding the reins when Hell says to him: “O `Ali! Your light is extinguishing my flames.” So, `Ali will say to it: “Calm down, Hell. Take so-and-so and leave so-and-so. Take this enemy of mine and leave this friend of mine.” On that day, Hell will be more obedient to `Ali than one of your servants will be to his master – if he wants, he can take it right, and if he wants, he can take it left. On that day, Hell will be more obedient to the orders of `Ali than all of creation.
